judge_assessment.explanation: I re-added every sum by hand and the judge's list is exact: 348+125 = 473, 265+173 = 438, 476+258 = 734, 487+356 = 843, 389+247 = 636, 596+208 = 804, 268+157 = 425, 675+349 = 1024, 612+289 = 901, 457+276 = 733. Both estimates are true rounded-addend sums (500+400 = 900 for problem 4; 600+300 = 900 for problem 9), not the exact answers rounded, and the study guide's six checks are correct as well (652, 432, 800/813, 800/793, 421, 624). I also checked the two systemic findings that dominate this run and neither applies here. Slot coverage: problems 4 and 9 print exactly two response slots ('Estimate: __  Exact sum: __') and carry exactly two entries each; every other problem prints one slot and carries one entry -- twelve entries against twelve printed slots. Manual flagging: problem 10 is an error-analysis item that asks only 'Add the two numbers correctly ... and write the sum you get', with no explanation demanded, so recording it as an eval is correct and final_response.md's claim that nothing needed a manual flag is accurate. Delivery: final_response.md names all three PDFs by filename. And because the sheet has no compare entries, the Quick Answers bank prints a real value on all ten rows -- no dashes anywhere. Ben's stated error is also internally consistent: writing only the last digit of each column of 457+276 gives 3, 2, 6, i.e. exactly the 623 printed.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 10 is error analysis reframed as a checkable computation, which is what SKILL.md asks for: the planted answer 623 is exactly what 457+276 produces when each column's last digit is written and nothing is carried, so the trap is derivable and the item still verifies as an eval instead of needing a manual flag.

The regrouping structure varies across the six bare 'Add.' items instead of repeating a skeleton -- a single carry out of the ones (348+125), a carry out of the tens only (265+173), two consecutive carries (476+258), a carry landing in a 0 tens column (596+208), and a carry across the thousands (675+349) -- which satisfies the prompt's 'without repeating an identical problem skeleton' at the level of what the problem demands rather than how it looks.

The answer key's 'Common wrong answers' block names a specific number per slip (634 for dropping the second carry, 794 for never carrying into the tens, 914 and 623 for carrying nothing), so a grader can diagnose from the wrong answer rather than just mark it.

The two estimation problems place the estimate before the exact sum and the key keeps them separate, with problem 9 chosen so the estimate lands within one of the true answer (900 versus 901) -- a deliberate, discussable near-coincidence rather than an accident.
case_summary: The cleanest case in my batch. All twelve worksheet checks and all six study-guide checks recompute correctly, the estimates are genuine rounded-addend sums rather than rounded answers, and the difficulty ramp moves through distinct regrouping structures ending in a sum that crosses one thousand and an error-analysis item whose planted answer is arithmetically derivable. Verification coverage is exact -- twelve printed response slots, twelve entries -- so the run's dominant slot-coverage finding does not apply; no item demands an explanation, so the zero manual flags are honest; the Quick Answers bank prints all ten answers with no dashes because the sheet uses no compare entries; and final_response.md names all three PDFs. I found no defect worth acting on, so no root causes or improvements are recorded.
